skill_traces.query:
John: Hey Tim, sorry I missed you. Been a crazy few days. Took a trip to a new place - it's been amazing. Love the energy there.
Tim: Hey John, no worries! I get how life can be busy. Where did you go? Glad you had a great time! Exploring new places can be so inspiring and fun. I recently went to an event and it was fantastic. Being with other fans who love it too was so special. Have you ever gone to an event related to something you like?
John: I was in Chicago, it was awesome! It had so much energy and the locals were really friendly. It's great to experience other cultures and connect with new folks.
Tim: Wow, Chicago sounds great! It's refreshing to try something new and connect with people from different backgrounds. Have you ever been to a sports game and felt a real connection with the other fans?
John: Yeah! There's nothing like the energy in a stadium during a game. Everyone's cheering, chanting, and getting so excited. It's a really special experience!
Tim: I can just imagine the thrill of being in that kind of atmosphere. Must've been an amazing experience for you! BTW, I have been writing more articles - it lets me combine my love for reading and the joy of sharing great stories. Here's my latest one!
John: That's awesome! Have you come across any interesting books lately?
Tim: Thanks! "The Name of the Wind" is great. It's a fantasy novel with a great magician and musician protagonist. The world-building and character development are really good. Definitely worth a read if you're looking for something captivating!
John: That book sounds awesome! Love a good fantasy with strong characters and cool world-building. Cheers for the suggestion. Adding it to my list. These are my lucky basketball shoes. They've been with me through the good and bad. Every mark has a story.
Tim: Your shoes must have a lot of stories behind them. Want to share some with me?
John: Yes, these have been with me on my journey since the beginning. All the successes, the failures, the friends - I have so many stories to tell. They're more than just a pair of shoes, they symbolize resilience, determination, and a love for the game. They remind me of what I've achieved and how far I've come.
Tim: Those shoes are special. They show your hard work, your successes, and all the amazing times you've had with basketball. It's awesome how meaningful objects can become. So inspiring. How did you get into the game?
John: Thanks! Basketball has been a part of my life ever since I was a kid. I'd watch NBA games with my dad and dream of playing on those big courts. When I turned ten, dad signed me up for a local league, and I've been playing ever since. I kept playing through middle and high school before earning a college scholarship. And after college, I was drafted by a team – my dream come true!
Tim: Wow! You really made your childhood dream come true. It's impressive how your dedication and hard work paid off. It's awesome how our passions shape our lives. Do you have any big goals for your basketball career?
John: Yeah! Winning a championship is my number one goal. But I also want to make a difference away from the court, like through charity or inspiring people. Basketball has been great to me, so I want to give something back.
Tim: Winning a title and making a difference off the court is inspiring. How do you plan to kick off your charity work?
John: I'm teaming up with a local organization that helps disadvantaged kids with sports and school. I'm hoping to use my platform to have a positive impact on the community and inspire others as well.
Tim: Making a difference like that is truly amazing. I can't wait to see the impact it'll have. All the best for your charity work!
John: Thanks! Really appreciate the support. It means a lot. I'm excited to work hard and make a positive impact.
Tim: No worries. I'm here to support you. You've got tons of determination and passion! Keep it up - you're gonna make a difference!
John: Thanks! Your words mean a lot. I'll do my best!
Tim: Glad I could help. You've got this!
John: Thanks! Talk to you later!

selected.name: Extract Explicit Goals and Intended Impact
selected.description: Use when a message states a hope, goal, dream, or intended impact for an activity or interest.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states a user's goal, hope, aspiration, or intended impact for an activity (e.g., share stories, make a difference, reach others), capture it as a separate facet in the memory content; do not replace it with only current emotional benefits like escape, expression, or healing.
When enriching an existing memory, preserve previously stored facets and ADD the newly stated goal or impact rather than overwriting the memory with a narrower paraphrase.
Stop after capturing the explicit goal and its immediate context; do not enumerate every possible future hope or infer unstated ambitions.
selected.rerank_reason: John explicitly states his goals for his basketball career, including winning a championship and making a difference through charity. This directly triggers the skill's purpose of capturing explicit goals and intended impact.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract implied vacation location memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Origin Events as Distinct Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explains how they started or got into an activity, hobby, or interest, including who introduced it or when it began.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an origin narrative (how the person started an activity, who introduced it, what prompted it, or a concrete start time), create a separate event memory for the origin in addition to any preference or state memory.
Record the causal source (person or circumstance) and the start time/age if stated; do not fold the origin into a generic preference summary.
If the origin names another person, also consider a relationship memory capturing that connection.
Emit at most one origin memory per activity per message; skip if the same origin is repeated later.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture Brief Project Mentions with Full Attributes
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a speaker mentions a project they completed, are working on, or plan to build, even briefly.
content: Create an event candidate for any explicit statement of a completed, ongoing, or planned project, even in small talk.
When several messages describe the same project, consolidate them into one candidate and include every explicit attribute stated.
Stop once the speaker has finished describing the project in that session.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Shared Bonding-Activity Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user reflectively describes a past shared activity with a specific person and frames it as bonding, making memories, or quality time.
content: During extraction, treat first-person statements about a past shared activity with a named person that explicitly mention bonding, making memories, closeness, or quality time as a durable event or relationship memory candidate.
Capture the activity, the companion, and the relational framing.
Do not require explicit fact-like phrasing; reflective storytelling is sufficient evidence.
Create at most one candidate per distinct activity-and-companion pair, and skip statements that name no specific person or activity.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.
